targets.from: judgement values from the drafter's reading of the sources and knowledge of the species (2026-11-04), no photographs measured; to be replaced by photo measurements: an airy, open shrub of bright green, angled stems and small leaves in flat sprays, see-through even in summer

young.note: a few green stems sprouting from a mossy stump or nurse log

old.note: a tall old shrub, the lower stems grey-brown, often perched on top of a huge old stump

description: An airy shrub of the rain forest, 1.5-4 m, built of bright green, sharply angled stems with small, thin, oval leaves, often growing out of the top of a rotting stump or nurse log. In late summer it hangs out translucent coral-red berries one by one along the twigs.

season_notes.winter: Mostly bare, but the green stems (and a few evergreen juvenile leaves) keep it green.
season_notes.spring: Small waxy greenish-pink urn flowers, April-June.
season_notes.summer: Bright red, tart berries about 8 mm, July-September.

range.where: conifer forest from sea level to about 1,500 m, west of the Cascades and Sierra (FEIS); southeast Alaska to central California

notes: Grown from coffeeberry (a broadleaf shrub with berries; the library has no deciduous Vaccinium) as a more open, airier shrub with tiny leaves and green stems. It is deciduous (mature leaves fall; juvenile leaves are evergreen and toothed; FEIS), so leaf_on_by_month is set rather than coffeeberry's evergreen year. Leaves 1-3 cm (drafter). Its habit of rooting on stumps, snags and nurse logs (FEIS) is the most telling thing about it and is not expressed: the generator roots plants on the ground, and it would need a 'perch' (a stump or log top) from the deadwood or nurse-log placement. Berries drawn single ('bud' form), not in clusters. FEIS: black bears seek the berries; black-tailed deer depend on it heavily in winter; it is important elk browse in fall in western Washington; thrushes, band-tailed pigeons and grouse eat the fruit; mountain beavers, raccoons and squirrels too. Only the bear, deer, Steller's jay and coyote are in the animal library.
